\caption{Run-to-run stability, \textbf{\texttt{\_only\_subset} corpus tier}. Five independent detector runs and six parser observations per state, all \texttt{-{}-no-cache}, split across two days: repeated runs within one session understate variance, and Nevada demonstrates it here --- its detector output has the same element set in all three same-session runs (one of them differing only in the Science domain's code) and drops one indicator in both next-day runs. \emph{ids} is the number of distinct element identities compared and \emph{unstable} how many differed in any graded field, so the rate is bounded in $[0,1]$. Four of six states are perfectly reproducible on each suite. \textbf{These rates are lower bounds, not estimates}: a defect that fires in a minority of runs survives five clean draws easily, which is why denominators are reported beside every rate.
